ground_truth.title: How Fast Do Electric Skateboards Go? Top Speeds Revealed
ground_truth.main_content:
The introduction of electric skateboards, more popularly known as e-boards, has revolutionized the experience of skating. This portable mode of transport also helps make shorter journeys more enjoyable.

These electrically controlled skateboards are designed to help you get the most incredible speed. So if you wish to get from one point to another really fast, an e-board is just what you need!

But exactly how fast do electric skateboards go?

This article will present detailed information about electric skateboards, their speed, and factors that affect the speed, along with some safety precautions.

How Fast Do Electric Skateboards Go

In most urban places, it is now customary to try new modes of transportation. With the rise in popularity of skateboards, they have become a must-buy portable means of transport. Most people choose electric skateboards because of their affordability, convenience, and portability.

However, the primary purpose of buying an electric skateboard is often just speed. So, whether you wish to race around for leisure or reach work on time, obviously, you’d want to go fast. So, how fast can an electric skateboard go?

Electric skateboards go from 18 to 28 miles per hour (29-45 km/h). However, the top speed differs from model to model as various factors affect the speed of an electric skateboard.

Some of the models can exceed the 40 miles per hour limit with improved wheels and motor power. Therefore, there isn’t a fixed average speed for every model. However, some high-quality electric skateboards can go beyond 40 mph.

Average Speed of Electric Skateboard

The speed depends on multiple factors: the components, specs, deck, motor power, wheel shape and size, the rider’s weight, etc. With these factors influencing the speed, some e-boards top 65 km/h. Therefore, if you compare them with traditional skateboards, they are faster for sure! But the average speed of every electric skateboard is around 18-28 mph.

A wireless hand-held remote controls the speed. There are different kinds of remotes with thumbwheels or thumb sliders. You can select to slide the thumbwheel forward or in reverse for backward motion.

The rider’s body weight shifting between the front and rear of the board also controls the speed. The front of the board promotes forward motion while the back controls the brake. The tilting of the board directs it to the right and left.

Can You Make Your Electric Skateboard Speedier?

Some technical factors, such as the build of your skateboard, play an essential role in making your e-board fast. However, there are some things that you can do to make your e-board go faster.

For instance, you will have to consider some factors such as harder wheels, battery, and voltage if you wish to make your e-board go faster.

You can increase the top speed by incorporating higher voltage batteries, bigger wheels, and tighter gearing.

1. Bigger Wheels

Bigger wheels are faster as they tend to have a higher top speed. Plus, they have more momentum and tend to roll longer than smaller wheels.

Although bigger wheels are harder to push, they roll for much longer. This feature helps with cruising, too.

Besides this, low-quality urethane wheels sag as they have poor rebound and also roll slowly. In contrast, high-quality wheels are made from durable urethane and have a high rebound with a strong core.

2. Hard Wheels

A hard tire rolls faster while squishy tires slug along and lose momentum. They do not allow you to achieve a maximum speed.

The wheels absorb energy when they pound the road, so if you’re going fast, your squishy tire wouldn’t be able to support your speed. Since hard wheels have more rebound, they reflect as much energy as they get. So they accelerate and tend to maintain momentum.

3. Steeper Roads

Harder wheels reflect more road vibration. So road imperfections, such as bumps, might affect your speed.

Moreover, road bumps reduce the momentum, slowing you down. Therefore, the rougher roads are considered undesirable for skating. So if you wish to go faster, it’s best to take a smoother road.

4. More Aerodynamic

Aerodynamics makes a big difference when it comes to your speed on an electric skateboard. To get more aerodynamics, you need to reduce your surface area. It is the reason behind skateboarders bending when they aim for more speed.

Like skating, the tucking position helps cut through the air. After that, you have to get your chest as close to your knee as possible to close off air pockets. Again, it may help increase your speed.

So changing the wheel size and quality, choosing a better and smoother terrain, being aware of aerodynamics, and positioning yourself may make a huge difference.

Factors Affecting Your Electric Skateboard’s Speed

Some contributing factors to your electric skateboard’s speed are the motor, rider’s weight and balance, and the shape and size of the wheels.

The material and the quality of the components also play an essential role in the speed of your e-board. For example, better quality components are durable and help you speed through rough terrains.

The most important factors that affect the electric skateboard’s speed are the motor and battery.

Motor

The crucial factor that determines the speed of an electric skateboard is the ratio of power to weight. Since the motor is the heart of the skateboard, it plays a vital role in determining the range and speed that you can achieve.

For example, if you want to achieve a maximum speed of 25 mph, you’ll need to upgrade the motor and power. It is why people recommend buying skateboards with durable and powerful motors.

The size of the motor and the power are directly proportional to the speed of your skateboard. Therefore, skateboards with larger motors will always be faster.

Battery and Voltage

For high-end electric skateboards, the battery’s importance cannot be overstated.

The battery’s power output is an essential factor that affects the speed of your electric skateboard, as the power output of the battery determines how much power is supplied to the motor. In addition, it changes how much power is sent to the wheels.

The more you use your motor, the faster you will go. However, this will also use up more energy. So when the battery begins to drain, the motor becomes less powerful, and you experience a voltage sag when accelerating.

In addition to this, the electric skateboard’s motor is built to use lithium-ion batteries. These batteries require a single charge. Therefore, a low battery percentage might affect the speed of your skateboard.

To combat this issue, make sure that your battery is fully charged before you try to achieve the maximum speed limit.

Final Thoughts

Electric skateboards have completely transformed how we move, offering speed, convenience, and excitement all in one ride. While most e-boards average between 18 and 28 mph, some high-performance models, like those from Ecomobl, can push well past 40 mph.

Your actual speed depends on factors such as motor power, battery capacity, wheel type, rider weight, and even road conditions. And while it’s tempting to chase maximum speed, it’s important to balance performance with safety.

With the right board, setup, and precautions, you can enjoy the thrill of fast rides while staying safe and in control.
